question_prompt: Your turn begins, no urgent threat needs an answer, and you have enough mana to act. What feels best?
primary_observation: Preference to advance a plan first or preserve resources to answer others.
adaptive_ask_when: Always; Gate 1.
do_not_ask_when: Never use alone for identity support.
jargon_help: Players use threat for a card, battlefield, or plan they believe they need to answer.

question_prompt: As play comes back around to you, which position usually feels more comfortable?
primary_observation: Preference for power visible on the battlefield or held in hand, mana, or other less visible zones.
adaptive_ask_when: Always; Gate 2.
do_not_ask_when: Do not infer actual threat level.
jargon_help: Board means the cards and tokens on the battlefield. Permanent means a card or token on the battlefield.

question_prompt: A board wipe—an effect that removes many cards and tokens from the battlefield—is likely next turn. What would you rather have prepared?
primary_observation: Preference to protect an established position, reduce exposure, or recover after broad disruption.
adaptive_ask_when: Always; Gate 3.
do_not_ask_when: Do not treat the answer as proof the deck is resilient.
jargon_help: A graveyard is a player's discard pile.

question_prompt: When your Commander deck is doing what you built it to do, how do you want the advantage to arrive?
primary_observation: Preference for repeated small gains, cycles, or one concentrated payoff.
adaptive_ask_when: Always; Gate 4.
do_not_ask_when: Do not infer game length or ending mode.

question_prompt: If your commander is removed twice, what should the rest of the deck still be able to do?
primary_observation: How much the deck should depend on its commander being available.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when commander reliance could separate remaining candidates.
do_not_ask_when: Do not test commander affection or deck quality.

question_prompt: Opponents have learned how to stop your main engine. When you revise the deck, what structure do you want next?
primary_observation: Whether revision preserves one central engine, replaces functions, overlaps modules, or preserves purpose while changing tools.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when engine structure remains a live separator and DG_C06 has not been observed.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask after another C06 observation; artifacts, machinery, redundancy, or toolbox play cannot establish Colorless or Yore.
jargon_help: An engine is a repeatable set of cards whose pieces create more value together than they do alone.

question_prompt: The player ahead uses all their mana and leaves one turn where the table can take control. Which kind of pressure do you want your deck to create?
primary_observation: The channel through which the player wants to turn one opening into progress toward ending the game.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when live candidates agree on proactive play but differ in coordinated, embodied, abundant, burst, restrictive, or engine pressure.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask after DG_C07 is observed; combat, a large turn, or a noncombat engine never establishes identity by itself.

question_prompt: If you can either spend most of your mana advancing your own plan or keep it available to answer opponents, which do you prefer?
primary_observation: Preference to commit mana on one's own turn or retain options during opponents' turns.
competitor_pair_or_family: Blue, Azorius, Esper, Jeskai, and cadence boundaries
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when Gate initiative leaves families close.
do_not_ask_when: Do not count independently from C01 when both describe one cadence.

question_prompt: Across several games with the same deck, how much do you want the path to your main plan to repeat?
primary_observation: Preference for familiar access to a central plan or greater game-to-game variance.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when candidates differ in repeatability.
do_not_ask_when: Do not reduce the answer to tutor count.

question_prompt: For one deck slot, assume you can’t get both: one card fits your theme better, while another does the same job more reliably. Which do you keep?
primary_observation: Willingness to keep thematic expression when a more reliable role-player exists.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when attachment may explain contradictory behavior answers.
do_not_ask_when: Do not use alone for identity support.
jargon_help: Here, theme means a chosen story, visual idea, creature type, or self-imposed concept.

question_prompt: If your board becomes the clearest threat, how do you want the deck to handle that attention?
primary_observation: Preference to avoid early attention, adapt to attention, or embrace being the visible threat.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when visibility separates candidates.
do_not_ask_when: Do not infer actual power or social conduct.
jargon_help: Players use threat for a card, battlefield, or plan they believe they need to answer. Board means the cards and tokens on the battlefield.

question_prompt: You can give up a useful permanent now for cards or another lasting resource. What feels natural?
primary_observation: Willingness to spend permanents, life, cards, or position as fuel for later advantage.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when candidates differ in voluntary conversion.
do_not_ask_when: Do not equate sacrifice with graveyard or Black identity.
jargon_help: Permanent means a card or token on the battlefield. Board means the cards and tokens on the battlefield.

question_prompt: The table agrees to stop a repeatable threat. Before your next turn, the board changes and that threat is weaker but still present. What should the agreement require now?
primary_observation: How a public agreement should persist or change after the board changes.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when public procedure, shared access, durable obligation, bounded coordination, or revisable influence separates the live frontier.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask when the player lacks a recognizable table-agreement context or DG_C13 is already observed; a deal preference cannot name an identity alone.
jargon_help: Repeatable means a card or engine that can create the same threat again if the table leaves it in place.

question_prompt: Your deck becomes much stronger after several setup turns, but the table is already developing threats. What must the setup do along the way?
primary_observation: What contribution a longer development plan must make while the current table continues to move.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when development horizon separates the live frontier and DG_C14 has not been observed.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask after another C14 observation; long setup, early help, or incremental value cannot establish an identity alone.
jargon_help: Setup means the turns and cards a plan needs before it can produce its main payoff.

question_prompt: Once you know what you want a deck to do, how much do you want the available cards to shape the challenge?
primary_observation: Preference for how much of the deckbuilding boundary should come from the available card pool versus restrictions the builder chooses within broader access.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when color-count families remain plausible after behavior evidence.
do_not_ask_when: Never assign a color-count identity from this answer.

question_prompt: An opponent begins a decisive turn, but you do not yet know which card matters most. When do you want your deck to use the card or mana it kept available?
primary_observation: The commitment point at which hidden information becomes sufficient to spend a held answer.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask when information use and interaction timing separate the live frontier and DG_C08 has not been observed.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask after another C08 observation; waiting, prevention, or split mana alone cannot establish a color or faction.

question_prompt: A dangerous opposing play has been stopped, and you now have enough cards to choose among several workable plans. What do you most want to do next?
primary_observation: After interaction or new card access creates several viable options, preference to consolidate one route, retain broad optionality, or exploit the current opening.
competitor_pair_or_family: Esper; Blue; Black; Azorius; Dimir; Grixis; Jeskai; control; combo; toolbox; midrange; tempo
adaptive_ask_when: Ask adaptively when remaining candidates differ in how new information becomes route commitment and at least two independent behavioral observations already exist.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask when no real choice among routes exists, when the result is already stable, or as proof of skill, archetype, or identity.

question_prompt: Your spell-heavy deck has mana for a major turn. Which payoff sounds more like the plan?
primary_observation: Preference for repeated small gains, cycles, or one concentrated payoff.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask only when UR/PRISMARI remain close after two independent observations.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask if spell-heavy behavior was never observed.
jargon_help: Spell-heavy means instants or sorceries are central to the deck. An engine is a card or group of cards that repeatedly helps your deck—for example by drawing cards, making mana or tokens, or building counters.

question_prompt: Several cards from your battlefield went to your graveyard. What do you want that loss to enable?

adaptive_ask_when: Ask only when BG/WITHERBLOOM remain close.
do_not_ask_when: Do not ask if graveyard use was never observed.
jargon_help: A graveyard is a player's discard pile.

adaptive_ask_when: Ask only when mono/multicolor candidates remain close after behavior evidence.
do_not_ask_when: Never permit a one-answer color-count flip.
jargon_help: Here, color count means the number of colors in the commander's color identity. Here, color roles are broad tool families associated with colors; no color-pie knowledge is required.

question_prompt: An opponent removes the piece your deck was built around after using most of their mana and cards. Your turn begins with the rest of your board still available. What do you try first?
primary_observation: The first response chosen after a central plan is removed while other board resources remain.
adaptive_ask_when: Ask only when disruption response is the highest-value unresolved boundary and DG_C03 detail can change the responsible result.
